q: Read Precious Little Sleep, started last night with a SWAP: 30 minute calming bedtime routine (nursed just prior to start of bedtime routine), then put down awake, staying in room and started humming/singing and butt pats/jiggling (my chosen SWAP) when he started crying.
cx: Breastfeeding mother of a room-sharing 7-month-old who wakes every 45 minutes to 2 hours.

q: He woke up again around 10:15, I would usually nurse him but following PLS rec about not nursing  before midnight, I did SWAP and he went back to sleep until 1:30.
cx: Night one following the book's rule.

q: I room share so respond pretty quickly, he can see me from his crib, it feels wrong to just lay there and ignore him for more than a couple minutes.
cx: Why the method is hard in a shared room.

q: In the MOTN, should I stick to the SWAP or just settle him however possible (rocking)? I’m going for consistency so I feel like I should SWAP but that had mixed results last night.
cx: One of five numbered questions after night one.

q: I was following a recommendation for older “motion junkies” baby from Precious Little Sleep. […] I didn’t want to try complete extinction because when left alone to cry in the past (he hates his car seat and I can’t soothe him while driving) he vomits on himself.
cx: Reply to a commenter who said the method did not suit his age.

q: Up until 4,5months she slept great from 8pm-5am then waking up continuing till 7am most of the time. […] All of a sudden overnight she completely changed. Started to resist bedtime getting much harder to sleep and everything regressing night by night.
cx: Breastfeeding mother of a 6-month-old, six weeks into a regression.

q: I tried gentle Ferber 3,5 with a maximum of 7min ( both in room and outside ) IT WAS HORRIBLE , she does not cry she screams hysterically not even trying to settle in any sort of way.
cx: The gentlest timed version still failed.

q: I tried with all kinds of last wake windows 2,5hours ,2hours ,3hours everything.she has days with more nap time with less nap time its all the same.
cx: Schedule changes made no difference.

q: We did a short round of sleep training at 6 months old which worked for a few months but he has lost the skill. It was easier to tolerate at 6 months because he couldn't stand up, and he only cried for 10 minutes 3 nights in a row before mostly sleeping through the night.
cx: Mother of a 15-month-old waking after nearly every sleep cycle.

q: My husband isn't willing to leave him to cry it out alone at this stage, and I'm on the fence. I'm not really wanting to convince my husband to do something that I'm not 100% sold on.
cx: Why they will not retrain with crying.

q: We currently rock/hold (dad/grandma) or nurse (mom) our 15 month old to sleep. It's hard on our bodies and we're wanting to transition to just laying down with him.
cx: Three caregivers settle him.

q: Please help. I can't do these short naps anymore. 7 months of it and I am exhausted and angry and so beside myself.
cx: Parent of a 7-month-old with 32- and 20-minute naps that day.

q: We don't want to do CIO, though we have done some because I simply need a break and am too frustrated to go in and get baby at the time.
cx: Reply about which training they would accept.

q:
I’ve tried to extend that but it makes things worse and no matter if I shorten or extend wake windows, every nap and bedtime consists of tears and has done so his entire life. 

Literally I’m lucky if I get a 2 hour stretch.
cx: Breastfeeding mother of an 11-month-old on 3/3/4.

q:
(Pumped a bottle, prepared my husband extensively, fed him and kept all wake windows perfect) and of course he refused to go to sleep in his crib.

I’m currently fully dressed for dinner sitting in a dark room with make up on holding my baby missing yet another celebration.
cx: Mother of a 6.5-month-old missing her best friend's birthday dinner.

q: I know this is probably a comfort and sleep association issue, but I'm finding it difficult to be the only person who can put him to sleep for every nap. I'm not willing to do cry-it-out.
cx: Mother of a 3-month-old who only falls asleep nursing; the father manages one carrier nap.

q: After a lot of back and forth and research, we have decided to sleep train. We have chosen the Ferber method, and tonight was night 2. After about 30 minutes of crying she is asleep. I’m just really needing some encouragement because it is so hard to listen to her cry.
cx: First-time mother posting on Ferber night 2.

q: I am unable to be the mother that I want to be because we have no routine and we are both exhausted and overstimulated by the end of the day.
cx: Why she chose to train.

q: I’m a SAHM and that usually makes people think I should be able to just go with the flow and do whatever she wants, but neither of us are thriving with that. We need some routine.
cx: What people assume about a stay-at-home mother.

q: I was so against it because of all of the negative talk about it, until I finally read the (admittedly very limited) research myself.
cx: How she changed her mind about training.

q: Being a mom is just a cycle of guilt I guess 🤣
cx: End of a reply about wanting to do her home role well.

q: I’ve been following her sleep cues fur naps until now, but I think it’s time to transition to set nap times and wake windows.
cx: Next morning, planning a fixed schedule.

q: We hit 6.5 months and it's like all hell broke loose. It started with LO screaming crying the second their butt touched the crib.
cx: Father of an 8-month-old who now sleeps 30 minutes in the cot.

q: Has anyone clawed their way back from similar situations at this age? Any tips?
cx: His ask.

q:
Night 1 went surprisingly well. Bedtime was much easier than expected and we felt really encouraged.  
Tonight (Night 2) has been a completely different story.
cx: Parent of an 11-month-old with a rocking association, using a stay-in-the-room method.

q:
How long did it take your baby to stop waking 1-2 hours after bedtime and needing to resettle?  
How long did it take to break a strong rocking-to-sleep association?
cx: Two of her numbered questions.

q: Would love to hear success stories because tonight is making me question everything. 😅
cx: Success stories as night-two support.

q:
Night 1: cried 40 mins  
Night 2: cried 15 mins  
Night 3: cried 3 mins  
Night 4: cried 29 mins, false started and cried another 8 mins  
Night 5: cried 35 mins so far
cx: Parent of a 5-month-old logs Ferber; night 5 nearly as bad as night 1.

q: The crying is so loud and hard. I am so upset. I really need some support right now please. Tell me it gets better. I feel like I’m going to be sick 😭
cx: Written during night 5.

q: How much crying at bedtime do you allow before changing schedule? Do you ever assist sleep after some time? How do you stay consistent?
cx: Same parent as an earlier post: trained at 4 months, now 8.5 months, loud bedtime crying again.

q: I let her CIO for 25 minutes a couple days ago, then last night be barely cried, but tonight we went back to screaming for 20 minutes and I caved in.
cx: The pattern over three nights.
